goal: Gather separate analyses of two subjects in parallel, concatenate them, then synthesize a direct comparison and recommendation.
rationale: Parallel fan-out captures each subject independently so neither analysis contaminates the other. A concat reduce assembles the evidence in a consistent order before the final llm_call synthesizes a crisp comparison and recommendation — demonstrating that authored parallel shapes reliably outperform single-shot compare prompts.

params.instruction: Identify and summarize the strengths and weaknesses of the FIRST subject in the user's comparison request. Focus only on the first subject; do not mention the second. Cover at least: core capabilities or advantages, notable limitations or risks, and any evidence or examples that support your assessment. Write in plain prose, 150-250 words.

Identify and summarize the strengths and weaknesses of the SECOND subject in the user's comparison request. Focus only on the second subject; do not mention the first. Cover at least: core capabilities or advantages, notable limitations or risks, and any evidence or examples that support your assessment. Write in plain prose, 150-250 words.

Using the combined evidence in upstream state (combined_evidence), produce a direct head-to-head comparison of the two subjects from the user's request. Structure your response as: (1) a comparison table or bullet list of key differences, (2) a clear recommendation identifying which option is preferable and under what conditions, and (3) a one-sentence justification grounded in the evidence. Be decisive — hedge only where the evidence genuinely requires it.
